name: Why employer branding? The business case
purpose: Why should a firm invest in its employer brand when talent is scarce?

parts.label: Manage the psychological contract
points: The brand shapes expectations about the employment deal

parts.label: Signal values and prestige
points: Signalling to job seekers: what it is like to work here, how people are treated

parts.label: Create common identity
points: A source of shared identity for current employees

apply: Name which of the three functions the case firm's brand fails at
Check whether the brand promise matches the employee experience (exit interviews, Glassdoor)
pitfalls: Treating employer branding as advertising only – it is about the employment deal and its delivery
example: Increasing labour-market competition for key talent makes the employer brand a strategic issue.

name: How to build an employer brand: 6 steps
purpose: Which steps lead from self-analysis to a distinctive, measured employer brand?

parts.label: 1. Who am I?
points: Corporate, product and employer brand aligned

parts.label: 2. Customers
points: Ask employees, survey the target population (Randstad)

parts.label: 3. Competitors
points: Map rivals by attribute: projects, career, learning, WLB, CSR, diversity…

parts.label: 4. Distinctive EVP
points: Attributes you most want to be associated with

parts.label: 5. Create & communicate
points: Social networks, universities, job sites, media

apply: Walk through the steps with case facts; steps 1–3 are the analysis, 4–6 the design
Spot the skipped step (often: no customer or competitor analysis)
pitfalls: Jumping to step 5 (a campaign) without steps 1–4
Promising what the identity cannot deliver
example: Lombard Odier: redesign the EVP for mid-career women starting from steps 1–3.

name: Identity vs image
purpose: Is the employer brand what we are – or what others see?

parts.label: Image – what others see
points: Perception of candidates and the market

apply: Compare the case firm's message (image) with what employees report (identity)
A gap = broken psychological contract → turnover
pitfalls: Fixing an identity problem with more marketing
example: A tech firm advertises “innovative and employee-centric” but exit interviews cite poor career progression – fix the experience, not the ads (exam 2025/26, MC 18).

name: Employee value proposition (EVP)
purpose: What value do employees get from working here? A holistic EVP has four parts.
apply: Rate the case firm's EVP on all four parts for its target group
Find what is distinctive vs competitors – “good pay” is not distinctive
pitfalls: An EVP that is true for one group (juniors, men) but not for another (mid-career women)
example: Randstad 2026: work-life balance ranks first for many groups; career progression remains a key reason to leave.

name: What makes a strong employer brand?
purpose: Four tests for the brand and its communication.

parts.label: Insightful
points: Connects with rational and emotional needs

apply: Test the case campaign on all four; consistency (promise = experience) is the most common failure
